purpose: Verified published figures for the R1.1 context block (input to T29). Every row lists, under 'support', the quote ids in quotes.json that back each part of the row; verify_quotes.py checks each quote verbatim and cross-checks the ids (quote_check.json). Figures stay with their own device, code and workload; none is a measurement of this paper.

rows.capacity_statement: The source calls 65 million elements 'the limit' for the Futhark implementation on the A100 [T16]. This is a rounded statement: the demonstrated 65,536,000-element mesh already exceeds 65e6 taken literally, so no exact maximum is inferred. Cite it as 'about 65 million elements, the stated limit' and give 640x320x320 as the demonstrated mesh.

released_code.note: cgmax = 200 in top3d.c is passed to top3dmgcg but never to the solver; the solver loop uses its own maxIter = 1000

released_code.value: recursive residual < 1e-3 x initial residual of the solve; cap 10000

released code: FP32 storage of input, output and vectors; within each of the 24 element-row kernels the products and sum are evaluated in FP64 (unsuffixed double literals) and rounded to FP32 on output; the 24 partial results are accumulated through FP32 storage
released_code.check: code_checks.json: 576 coefficient literals, none f-suffixed; NVRTC PTX of each kernel body, compiled in a stand-in function with CuPy's declared argument types, has FP64 instructions in 24/24 kernels as released and in 0/24 with f-suffixed literals. This shows how the released expressions compile in that wrapper; it cannot establish which arithmetic ran in the published benchmarks.
released_code.published_account: Hou et al. state: 'The sensitivities are processed in double precision, and all other data are processed in single precision.' [H22]. The released kernels differ from that account in their internal arithmetic.
